blocks.text: Setting up Chrome for digital product testers on Mac

Your browser is your primary tool. A cluttered Chrome setup slows down your testing cycles. Start by creating dedicated Chrome profiles for every project. Go to the Profile icon in the top right corner and select Add. This keeps your cookies and extensions separate for each client or app you test. Use a clean profile for every new test suite to ensure a neutral environment.

items: Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab instantly.
Use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow to switch between open tabs.
Use ⌘ + L to jump to the address bar for quick navigation.
Use ⌘ + Shift + Delete to clear your browsing data when you need a fresh start.

blocks.text: Testers spend a significant portion of their day updating Jira tickets or Notion docs. You can dictate your findings while you look at the screen. Hold the fn key to dictate your bug report. Speak clearly as you observe the defect. Lazur types the text directly into your browser fields. This saves you from switching windows back and forth.

When a page fails to load, you often need to check the console or clear cache. If you encounter an Aw, Snap! error, check your network connection first. If it persists, use the Developer Tools by pressing ⌥ ⌘ I. You can also clear site data for one website in Chrome on Mac to resolve persistent session conflicts without logging out of your other apps.

If you are unsure where a specific setting is located in the Chrome menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur. It will circle the button or menu item on your screen so you can find it without searching through deep submenus.
blocks.title: Finding settings quickly

blocks.text: You do not need to manually track every small task. Ask Lazur to set a timer when you start a long regression test. Use it to create reminders for your next meeting. By offloading these small tasks to your voice assistant, you maintain your focus on the actual test execution. This is helpful for testers who manage multiple tickets simultaneously.

faq.question: How do I keep my Chrome testing environment clean?
faq.answer: Create a separate Chrome profile for each project. This ensures that cookies, cache, and extensions from one project do not interfere with another.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to document bugs while testing?
faq.answer: Yes. While you test in Chrome, hold the fn key to dictate your notes or bug descriptions directly into your bug tracking tool like Jira.

faq.question: How do I fix memory issues in Chrome?
faq.answer: Check your extensions and remove any that are not necessary. You can also use the Chrome Task Manager by going to Window > Task Manager to see which tabs are using the most memory.
